comments.text:
There’s a famous saying about GDP that goes like this. 

Two economists walk into the woods. As they do, one of them spots a pile of shit in their way and tells the other “I’ll pay you $200 to eat that.” The other economist agrees, and eats the pile of shit and takes the $200. 

As they continue walking, the economist who at the shit stumbles on another pile of shit and tells his friend “I’ll pay you $200 to eat that pile of shit.” The man agrees, eats the shit and gets paid $200. On that day, the GDP rose by $400. 

No one’s life improved just because someone ate shit and $200 was exchanged twice.

comments.text: I work as a trucker. I make double what my dad made while I was growing up, live in a lower cost of living area than he did, and have less debt than he did at my age. I pay almost double what he did to rent a smaller, much older house, have a car that was made before the truck he drove when I was in highschool, my only monthly bills outside of utilities are phone and internet, I spend on average 200 bucks a month on entertainment and other miscellaneous purchases. Even living modestly like this, I can't afford a house, a new car, or even vacations, let alone luxury purchases. Yet my dad had a motorcycle, a pair of jet skis, we went on vacations twice a year, and had a huge amount of savings. This is just patently unsustainable.

Yes it's been almost two decades and prices change, but the percentages of our paychecks that need to get split for things is out of whack and not sustainable if prices keep increasing. 30% of people's pay should be toward housing, not 50-70%. comments.text:
What I hate is it's almost impossitble to navigate your life. I was on medicaid, got a new job I knew paid enough I didn't qualify anymore, updated medicaid and they never replied to me after 45 days. So I had to waste a day trying to contact medicaid by phone to tell them, what the hell I shouldn't be on it. Then I had to send them pay stubs to show them I shouldn't be on it, and that took them 2 months to get to. The whole time I was stressed  using my card because it felt illegal to use it. But I couldn't get other insurance until they took me off. 

After I got off I had to contact the marketplace. The marketplace needed info my HR didn't know. So I had to contact a seprate company about what my company offers. I had to leave like 5 voice mails for days for them to call me. Then I finally could get insurance from the marketplace. 


Why the hell is it so hard. If I didn't stay on top of it all I'd probably be on mediciad illegally until I was fined big, even though I updated them correctly online. And the HR not knowing what my company offered almost made me give up getting insurance.

comments.text:
My mom is staunchly MAGA and I am very opposite her. She was saying how she doesn't understand how I am always struggling to afford groceries... while she actively also uses our town's food pantry. I explained that it isn't just the price going up (though I have seen that too) but quantities going down. I have a set walmart order i place each month with our essentials, and comparing past receipts, the price is substantially higher than a year ago, while we also have to order more often because some quantities dropped by ounces, pounds, or counts. 12 tortillas became 10, 5 lbs of rice became 2 for the same price, etc... if she is only comparing the price, she may see a small change, but to make a 1:1 for amounts? The price is so much higher now. And my income? It's only $20/month higher than it was this time last year. It cannot compete. Not when you factor in gas, etc.

The hardest part is the disconnect. My mom staunchly believes there hasn't been a change as fox news tells her everything is *fine*... but when she is getting to the checkout, it is hurting, and she cannot wrap her head around it.
comments.author: @Mamaplusone

comments.text:
Two economists are walking in a forest when they come across a pile of shit.

The first economist says to the other “I’ll pay you $100 to eat that pile of shit.” The second economist takes the $100 and eats the pile of shit.

They continue walking until they come across a second pile of shit. The second economist turns to the first and says “I’ll pay you $100 to eat that pile of shit.” The first economist takes the $100 and eats a pile of shit.

Walking a little more, the first economist looks at the second and says, "You know, I gave you $100 to eat shit, then you gave me back the same $100 to eat shit. I can't help but feel like we both just ate shit for nothing."

"That's not true", responded the second economist. "We increased the GDP by $200!"
